entries.sense_en: rising high above and seeming to rule the land around, like a proud master
entries.sense_ko: 주위를 굽어보며 군림하듯 우뚝 서 있는

synonyms.nuance: Purely about height; no idea of ruling or pride.
synonyms.example: The peak towers over the town.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral and common: has the strongest presence or control over a place or people.
Informal; about people giving orders, not places.
synonyms.example: He likes to boss his sister around.

entries.modern: "lording it over" → "towering over" (for places) / "acting superior to" (for people)
entries.tip_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 '잘난 척하며 군림하다'라는 부정적 뜻이 됩니다.

entries.sense_en: caught sight of something far away
entries.sense_ko: 먼 곳의 것을 알아보다, 멀리서 발견하다

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word: notice something quickly, near or far.
synonyms.example: I spotted her in the crowd.

synonyms.nuance: Suggests effort: see or read something unclear or distant.
synonyms.example: I could just make out a small boat.

synonyms.nuance: Literary, like descry; a sudden sighting of something hard to see.
synonyms.example: She espied a sail on the horizon.

entries.tip_ko: describe(묘사하다)와 철자가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 단어입니다.

entries.sense_en: the fact of being very old; great age

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for how old something is; says nothing about being impressive.
synonyms.example: The age of the house surprised us.

synonyms.nuance: Rare and plain; can sound neutral or negative, not respectful.
Stresses the feeling of being extremely old; rarer and less formal than antiquity.

entries.tip_ko: '고대'(ancient times)라는 뜻으로도 쓰이지만 여기서는 '오래됨'입니다.

entries.sense_en: controlled and nagged constantly by one's wife

synonyms.nuance: Only the constant complaining; does not say the husband is controlled.
Bullied into obeying by harsh words; stronger and not limited to marriage.
Idiom: completely controlled by another person, often a partner.

entries.tip_ko: hen(암탉)이 쪼는 모습에서 나온 말로, 남편에게만 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a gentle, quiet nature that never argues or resists

synonyms.nuance: Not thinking oneself important; a virtue, and it does not mean giving in to others.
synonyms.example: She accepted the prize with humility.

synonyms.nuance: Comes from fear or shyness, not from a gentle character.
Readiness to obey others; more clearly negative than meekness.

entries.tip_ko: meek는 긍정·부정 양쪽으로 쓰이지만 대체로 '힘없이 순종적인' 느낌이 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: too eager to please or obey people, in a way that seems false

synonyms.nuance: Acting like a servant with no will of one's own; stronger, more contemptuous.
Flattering someone to win favor; focuses on the flattery.
Ordinary good manners; obsequious is polite to an embarrassing, insincere degree.

entries.tip_ko: '예의 바른'이 아니라 '비굴할 만큼 굽실대는'이라는 부정적 단어입니다.

entries.sense_en: a bad-tempered, nagging woman
entries.sense_ko: 잔소리 심한 앙칼진 여자, 바가지 긁는 아내

synonyms.nuance: Anyone who keeps complaining; milder, also used of men and of horses.
Old-fashioned; a woman who keeps criticizing loudly.
synonyms.example: She was known as a scold.

synonyms.nuance: Very literary; a violent, overbearing woman, stronger than shrew.

entries.tip_ko: 쥐처럼 생긴 작은 동물 '뒤쥐'도 shrew입니다. 여기서는 사람을 뜻합니다.

entries.sense_en: easily bent or influenced; ready to give way

synonyms.nuance: Common word: bends easily or can change; usually a positive trait.
Goes along with rules or requests; focuses on obeying.
Easily shaped or influenced; used of metal, or of a person's mind.

entries.sense_en: small, noisy arguments about unimportant things

synonyms.nuance: General word; can be serious and lasting.
Very short, slight disagreement between people who are close.
A brief, angry quarrel over something small; slightly informal.

entries.sense_en: freedom from any punishment or bad result
entries.sense_ko: 벌을 받지 않음, 아무 탈이 없음

synonyms.nuance: Official protection from punishment or disease; a legal or medical status.
Being excused from a rule or duty, not necessarily from punishment.
Informal idiom: escaping a punishment one deserved.

entries.tip_ko: 'with impunity'(벌 받지 않고)의 형태로 가장 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a strong dislike that makes you want to avoid something

synonyms.nuance: The mildest and most common word.
Mild disapproval or disgust, often about manners or behavior.
Much stronger: deep hatred and disgust.

entries.tip_ko: 'aversion to + 명사' 형태로 씁니다 (aversion for도 가능).

entries.sense_en: steady, careful hard work over time

synonyms.nuance: More common; careful, conscientious effort at a task.
Continuing despite difficulty; stresses not giving up.
Formal: habit of hard work; the sense 'industry' as business is different.

entries.sense_en: walking slowly and with heavy steps, tired but continuing

synonyms.nuance: Slow, heavy, steady walking; suggests dull effort more than tiredness.
Relaxed, pleasant walking; the opposite feeling from trudge.
Walk a long way with firm steps, often through rough places.

entries.sense_en: so annoying and troublesome that it seems cursed (humorous exaggeration)

synonyms.nuance: Very bad or miserable; used for poor quality or unhappy conditions.
Old-fashioned mild curse word for something irritating.
Plain, modern, and much weaker.

entries.tip_ko: 원래 '전염병(pestilence)을 일으키는'이라는 뜻이며, 여기서는 과장해서 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: gradually became smaller in size or amount

synonyms.nuance: Get smaller, often suddenly or physically; can be quick.
synonyms.example: The sweater shrank in the wash.

synonyms.nuance: Get lower in quality, number or strength; neutral and formal.
Slowly lose strength, color or brightness until almost gone.

entries.tip_ko: 스스로 줄어드는 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓰지 않습니다.

entries.sense_en: a small, untidy, mischievous boy

synonyms.nuance: Playful and affectionate: a child who causes harmless trouble.
Mischievous person, child or adult, said with affection.
Stresses dirty, ragged clothes rather than bad behavior.

entries.tip_ko: sea urchin(성게)과 같은 단어입니다.

entries.sense_en: found it very hard to do something

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and modern; the usual way to say it.
synonyms.example: I had trouble finding the house.

synonyms.nuance: Stresses effort and difficulty, often with some failure.
Informal; suggests an unpleasant, tiring effort.
synonyms.example: She had a hard time explaining.

entries.modern: "had much ado to hold up" → "had a hard time holding up"
entries.tip_ko: 셰익스피어의 'Much Ado About Nothing'(헛소동)의 ado와 같은 말입니다.

entries.sense_en: repeating something loudly and again and again until the person is tired of it

synonyms.nuance: Keep talking about the same subject in a boring way.
synonyms.example: She kept harping on his mistakes.

synonyms.nuance: Repeat something to make someone learn or remember it.
Keep asking or complaining to make someone act.
synonyms.example: She nagged him about the dishes.

entries.tip_ko: dining(식사)이 아니라 din(소음)의 -ing형입니다.

entries.sense_en: having no better choice, so forced to do it

synonyms.nuance: Made to do something by duty or need; modern and neutral.
Forced by strong pressure; stronger than fain.
Ready to do something; fain here is willing only because nothing else is possible.

entries.modern: "was fain to" → "had no choice but to"
entries.tip_ko: fain은 원래 '기꺼이'라는 뜻이지만, 옛 표현 'was fain to + 동사원형'은 '(달리 방법이 없어) …할 수밖에 없었다'로 읽습니다.

entries.sense_en: a follower or supporter

synonyms.nuance: Plain, common word for someone who backs a person or team.
Someone who follows a leader or belief, sometimes without thinking.
A committed student of a teacher or belief; more devoted.

entries.sense_en: looking sideways, secretly or nervously

synonyms.nuance: Just the direction; has no feeling of secrecy or fear.
Secret and guilty in manner; may not involve looking sideways.
Slanting or indirect; formal, used for angles and hints.

entries.tip_ko: 'sidelong glance'(곁눈질) 형태로 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: red and healthy-looking in the face

synonyms.nuance: Common literary word: red and healthy, from sun or outdoor life.
Red, sometimes from drink or high blood pressure; less healthy.
Pink and healthy; softer and gentler, often for cheeks.

entries.sense_en: made afraid or discouraged by something difficult

synonyms.nuance: Frighten someone, usually on purpose, so they act or stay quiet.
synonyms.example: He tried to intimidate the witness.

synonyms.nuance: Take away someone's hope or wish to continue; less fear involved.
Make someone lose calm or confidence, often suddenly.

entries.tip_ko: 'not to be daunted by …'(…에 기죽지 않는) 형태로 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a small private group that meets to discuss and decide things together

synonyms.nuance: A closed group of friends who shut others out; usually negative.
A secret group plotting something, especially in politics.
Neutral: a group with a shared interest or job.

entries.tip_ko: 스페인어식으로 '훈토'라고 읽는 사람도 있지만 영어에서는 /ˈdʒʌntoʊ/입니다.

entries.sense_en: in a very strong, forceful and angry way

synonyms.nuance: With wild, strong energy; for feelings, fights and wind.
With deep emotion, often positive: love, belief, or argument.
Plain, general intensity; does not suggest anger.

entries.tip_ko: 'vehemently deny'(강력히 부인하다)로 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: approval, especially a sign of satisfaction

synonyms.nuance: Common everyday word for saying something is good or allowed.
Spoken or written admiration; warmer than approval.
Public support, e.g. from a famous person or group.

entries.sense_en: driven away from a place by force

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase: force someone to leave.
Beat an opponent in a contest or battle; no idea of running away.
Beat completely and easily; stronger, and not about fleeing.

entries.tip_ko: route(길)와 철자가 비슷하지만 다른 단어입니다. rout는 항상 /raʊt/(라우트)로 읽습니다.

entries.sense_en: a loud, bossy, angry woman

synonyms.nuance: Bad-tempered, bossy older woman; even more insulting.
Violent, overbearing woman; another literary word, close to virago.
Informal; a tough, intimidating older woman.

entries.tip_ko: 여성에 대한 모욕적 표현이므로 실제 대화에서는 쓰지 않습니다.

entries.sense_en: in a sad, longing way, wishing for something out of reach

synonyms.nuance: With a strong wish for something; not always sad.
synonyms.example: She looked longingly at the cake.

synonyms.nuance: Just unhappy; no sense of wishing for something.
Fondly, about the past.

entries.sense_en: a miserable life full of hard treatment and little pleasure
entries.sense_ko: 개 같은 삶, 고달프고 비참한 생활

synonyms.nuance: Formal way to say a very unhappy life.
Plain and neutral: difficulty, not necessarily cruelty.
Different: tiring competitive working life, not ill treatment.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 'lead a dog's life'는 '고생스럽게 산다'는 뜻으로 그대로 쓰입니다.

entries.sense_en: a small round hill

synonyms.nuance: A very small hill; nearly the same, a bit more common.
A pile or raised heap, natural or man-made.
Any raised land; larger and more general than knoll.

entries.tip_ko: k는 소리 나지 않습니다: /noʊl/.

entries.sense_en: a very steep cliff edge

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; a steep rock face, especially by the sea.
A rough, steep rock, usually in mountains.
Informal, focuses on the vertical fall itself.

entries.tip_ko: 'on the edge of a precipice'는 '위기의 벼랑 끝'이라는 비유로도 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a narrow valley between hills

synonyms.nuance: General word; usually wider than a glen.
Northern English, a wider open valley; poetic.
Deep, steep-sided, rocky valley; more dramatic than a glen.

entries.sense_en: hanging over the place, seeming about to fall
entries.sense_ko: 곧 덮칠 듯 튀어나온, 머리 위에 걸린

synonyms.nuance: Physically sticking out above; the direct, literal word.
Appearing large and threatening, often in fog or darkness.
About to happen in time; abstract events, not physical objects.

entries.tip_ko: 지금은 주로 시간적으로 '임박한'(impending disaster)의 뜻으로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: moved quietly and fearfully, keeping low to stay unseen

synonyms.nuance: Move quietly so as not to be noticed; may be playful.
Wait hidden, usually with a bad purpose; stays in place.
synonyms.example: A man was lurking in the alley.

synonyms.nuance: Crouch down in fear; no idea of moving stealthily.
synonyms.example: The dog cowered under the table.

entries.sense_en: an uneasy feeling that something bad may happen

synonyms.nuance: Stronger: deep fear of something certain to come.
synonyms.example: She felt dread on Monday mornings.

synonyms.nuance: A mild, vague worry with no clear cause.
Ongoing worry, from everyday nerves to a medical condition.

entries.tip_ko: '이해'나 '체포'라는 뜻도 있지만 이 문장에서는 '불안감'입니다.

entries.sense_en: quick and cheerful readiness to help or act

synonyms.nuance: Strong wish to do something; not about speed.
Doing something on time or at once; not necessarily willing.
Being prepared and willing; more neutral and calm.

entries.tip_ko: 'with alacrity'(기꺼이 재빨리)로 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a narrow channel worn into a hillside by water

synonyms.nuance: A deeper, larger valley with steep sides.
American: a deep, narrow valley cut by a fast stream.
A narrow channel dug by people, along a road or field.

entries.sense_en: mixed with gray; going gray with age

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for the color; no sense of age or toughness.
Very old-looking, white or gray; literary.
Shiny gray-white; sounds beautiful, not rough.

entries.tip_ko: grizzly bear(회색곰)와 같은 어원의 단어입니다.

entries.sense_en: strange and old-fashioned in an interesting way

synonyms.nuance: Just out of date; neutral or slightly negative.
Pretty enough for a picture; used for views and villages.
Strange or odd, without the charm of old age.

entries.tip_ko: 'quaint village'는 칭찬이지만 사람의 생각에 쓰면 '구식이다'라는 얕보는 말이 될 수 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: strange and rough-looking, not refined

synonyms.nuance: Rude, or roughly made; stronger and more insulting.
Rough in manners, speech or texture.
Plain word: not smooth or gentle, in looks or behavior.

entries.tip_ko: 'uncouth manners'처럼 예의 없는 태도에 흔히 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: drank a lot quickly and with enjoyment

synonyms.nuance: Swallow fast in big mouthfuls, often from hurry or thirst.
The opposite: drink in tiny amounts.
Drink greedily and noisily; often disapproving.

entries.sense_en: people who enjoy noisy, drunken fun

synonyms.nuance: Anyone celebrating loudly at a party; neutral.
Emphasis on heavy drinking.
Modern and neutral: a person at a party.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 철자는 roisterer입니다.

entries.sense_en: managed to do something with difficulty, using what was available

synonyms.nuance: The modern, everyday word: succeed despite difficulty.
Survive with just enough; not a single action.
synonyms.example: We can get by on little.

synonyms.nuance: Accept something less than ideal and use it anyway.
synonyms.example: We made do with old chairs.

entries.tip_ko: 명사 makeshift(임시변통의)의 뿌리가 되는 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: extremely hungry

synonyms.nuance: Informal and very common exaggeration for very hungry.
Hungry and eager to eat a lot.
The plain word; much weaker.

entries.tip_ko: famine(기근)과 같은 어원입니다.

entries.sense_en: mock someone in a rude, scornful way

synonyms.nuance: Make fun of someone, often by copying them.
Show contempt with the face or voice.
Shout rude, mocking remarks, usually in a group.

entries.tip_ko: 'scoff at + 대상'으로 씁니다. 영국 영어의 '게걸스레 먹다'는 별개 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: confused and muddled the mind

synonyms.nuance: Mix things up so they are unclear.
Confuse, often because of drink or tiredness.
The everyday word; general.

entries.modern: "has addled my head" → "has muddled my head"
entries.tip_ko: '썩은 달걀'(addled egg)에서 나온 말입니다.

entries.sense_en: empty and sad-looking, as if left behind

synonyms.nuance: Empty, bleak and lifeless; stronger, for places.
Unhappy from being alone; common, not necessarily abandoned.
Just empty of people; no sadness in it.

entries.sense_en: badly made or old, and likely to fall apart

synonyms.nuance: Moves or trembles; not steady (also used for voices).
Informal; rocks from side to side.
Worn out and falling apart because of long neglect; for buildings.

entries.sense_en: of long ago; from the old days

synonyms.nuance: Equally literary: in past times.
Everyday and plain.
Adjective for a past era, often with nostalgia.

entries.tip_ko: 'days of yore'(옛날) 형태로 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a calm, slow, unexcitable nature

synonyms.nuance: Staying calm under pressure; a positive quality.
Showing little feeling or interest; neutral or negative.
Plain, everyday word for a peaceful state.

entries.tip_ko: g는 소리 나지 않아 /flɛm/입니다. '가래'라는 뜻이 일반적이나 여기서는 '침착한 기질'입니다.

entries.sense_en: strange, confusing language that one cannot understand
entries.sense_ko: 알아들을 수 없는 말, 뜻 모를 소리

synonyms.nuance: Meaningless nonsense talk.
synonyms.example: Their words were gibberish to me.

synonyms.nuance: Informal: the special words of a group, often humorous.
Informal words used in casual speech by a group.

entries.tip_ko: 'Babylonish jargon'은 '바벨탑처럼 알아들을 수 없는 말'입니다.

entries.sense_en: with the hand on the hip and the elbow pointing out
entries.sense_ko: 손을 허리에 짚고 팔꿈치를 벌린 자세로

synonyms.nuance: The everyday description of the same pose.
synonyms.example: She stood with her hands on her hips.

synonyms.nuance: A different pose: arms crossed over the chest.
synonyms.example: He stood with his arms folded.

entries.modern: "with one arm akimbo" → "with one hand on his hip"
entries.tip_ko: 'arms akimbo'는 자신만만하거나 위압적인 자세입니다.

entries.sense_en: stern and serious; not friendly

synonyms.nuance: Serious and strict, expecting obedience.
Harsh and unkind; sometimes cruel.
Insists that rules be followed; about behavior, not appearance.

entries.tip_ko: 장식 없이 소박한 삶·건물에도 씁니다 (austere life).

entries.match: put their tongues in their cheeks
entries.headword: put one's tongue in one's cheek
entries.sense_en: showed by a facial sign that they did not believe him
entries.sense_ko: 혀로 볼을 밀어 믿지 않는다는 표시를 하다

synonyms.nuance: Close one eye quickly as a secret signal.
Smile in a self-satisfied or mocking way.

entries.modern: "put their tongues in their cheeks" → "smirked in disbelief"
entries.tip_ko: 현대의 'tongue-in-cheek'(농담 삼아 한 말)과는 조금 다르게 쓰인 옛 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: so worried and confused that he did not know what to do

synonyms.nuance: Not knowing what to say or do; milder, less desperate.
synonyms.example: I'm at a loss for words.

synonyms.nuance: Ready to try anything; more intense and general.

synonyms.word: at the end of one's rope
synonyms.nuance: American: out of patience or strength to continue.
synonyms.example: I'm at the end of my rope.

entries.tip_ko: wit's는 소유격 's입니다.

entries.sense_en: pleasant to look at, healthy and attractive

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word, usually for women and girls; plain and modern.
Neutral, for any person or thing.
Good-looking, mostly for men; for women suggests strong features.

entries.sense_en: supported a story by saying it was true

synonyms.nuance: Say or show that something is true; the general word.
Informal: support someone's story or claim.
Check that something is correct, e.g. facts or an identity.

entries.tip_ko: 다른 증거·증인이 있어서 '뒷받침한다'는 느낌이 강합니다.

entries.sense_en: a period of staying awake to watch or keep guard

synonyms.nuance: Plain word: guarding or observing over a period of time.
Staying with a dead person before the funeral.
A person or post used to watch for danger.

entries.tip_ko: 'candlelight vigil'(촛불 집회)처럼 조용한 추모·시위에도 씁니다.

entries.match: To make a long story short
entries.headword: to make a long story short
entries.sense_en: to sum up quickly without giving all the details

synonyms.nuance: Formal, brief: introduces a summary.
Casual, spoken shortening of the same idiom.
Informal: expressing the main point very briefly.

entries.sense_en: a state of being asleep or nearly inactive

synonyms.nuance: Extreme tiredness and lack of energy; often from illness or boredom.
Slowness and weak movement or activity.
Half-conscious daze, often from drink, drugs or shock.

entries.sense_en: something that heavily controls and burdens people, like a wooden bar on an ox

synonyms.nuance: A heavy duty or worry; not necessarily forced by another.
Slavery, or complete lack of freedom; stronger.
Figurative: things that restrict freedom.

entries.tip_ko: 'throw off the yoke'(속박을 벗어던지다)는 독립·해방을 뜻하는 표현입니다. yolk(노른자)와 발음이 같습니다.

entries.sense_en: slightly crazy; not thinking clearly

synonyms.nuance: Forgetful and unable to focus, in a harmless way.
Changing loyalties or opinions often; about commitment.
Mentally or emotionally unbalanced; serious and clinical.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 주로 '변덕스럽고 경솔한'이라는 뜻으로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: remember completely, word for word

synonyms.nuance: Make an effort to fix something in memory; the action.
British variant of the same idiom.
synonyms.example: She knew the song off by heart.

synonyms.nuance: Say aloud from memory, usually in front of others.

entries.tip_ko: 'by memory'가 아니라 'by heart'라고 합니다.
